# Ferrier's Fen · Book II, pp. 116–125
# Generated by the extractor — fix the extractor, not this file.
PAGE	116
P	Ferrier's Fen lies between the <b>Great Wood</b> (page 200), the <b>Steplands</b> (page 372), and the <b>North Manmarch</b> (page 282).
P	It's a huge wetland, 100 miles wide, 50 miles north to south, fed by the <b>Stream</b> (page 396) the Sruth near <b>Marshedge</b> (page 274), and many smaller creeks. It's a maze of firm ground, stagnant pools, shallow streams, and plunging drops into deep deep water. And mud. So much mud.
P	Long ago, this area was the cradle of <b>the</b> <b>Green Lords'</b> civilization (page 210). But when their servants rebelled and the Green Lords embraced the <b>Things Below</b> (page 412), the other <b>Makers</b> (page 264) collapsed the region and shattered the Green Lords' civilization. It's still a broken place, oozing with old magic and corruption.
H2	Impressions
HR
H3	Always
B	Willow trees leaning over water
B	Chunks of stone ruins, jutting from the mud
B	Wobble and shake of peat bogs underfoot
B	Sulphur smell of stagnant water and rot
B	Some mundane thing but shockingly wrong: a tree with weeping eyes, a three-faced rabbit, a snake with stumpy legs, a deer with a fawn growing from its side, etc.

B	Thick fog, muffling everything, shrinking the world

H2	Exploring the Fen
HR
P	Ferrier's Fen holds much of value, but it's a shifting, treacherous place.
H3	Chart a Course
P	On any expedition into Ferrier's Fen:
C	Choose 1:
B	You need to bring a pouch of ◇ bendis root (Value 1 in Marshedge) per day, burnt constantly
B	The way will be perilous, filled with dangers
C	You need a knowledgeable guide, like a <b>fen-walker</b> (next column)
C	You risk getting lost nonetheless
C	The terrain itself is treacherous; you risk injury along the way
C	The way will be grueling; you risk exhausting yourselves/your resources
C	You risk contracting <b>fen blight</b> (page 123)
C	You risk drawing the attention of the suarachan (except in winter)

PAGE	120
H2	The Willow Witches
HR
P	Many tales are told of the weird sisters of the Fen. There are always three, but they might be old, young, or middling aged.
P	They might be tall and regal or twisted and gnarled, dignified and poised or feral things rooting through the mud. Sometimes, the tale's hero seeks them out. Other times, they stumble upon the Witch's abode.
P	All stories agree that the Willow Witches have what you seek. An answer. An artifact (or knowledge of where to find it). A way to accomplish some impossible deed. Everyone knows that Sianna Ferrier learned the secrets of the Fen from the Witches, allowing Marshedge to be settled.
P	What the tales often fail to mention is:
P	there's always a price. For Sianna Ferrier, the Witches' gifts were costly indeed: a child of her blood, or the blood of those she settled with, to be delivered every seven years.
P	The witches are, in truth, a single entity, the inscrutable <b>incarnation</b> (page 300) of a primordial being of knowledge, fate, costs and consequences, greatly diminished and dwelling in this broken land.
H3	The Witches' abode
P	The Willow Witches' abode is rarely found in the same place twice, and in every tale, the details are different. Sometimes they dwell in the hollow of a willow tree, the space inside impossibly big. In other tales, it's a crude shack leaning against a tree. In still others, they huddle around a cookfire in a willow's shade, no real shelter to speak of.
P	The surest way to find the Witches is to seek out a <b>fen-troll</b> (page 123) and convince them to guide you. They all know the way, though one should expect mischief.
H3	Mind your manners
P	The Willow Witches observe the old ways of hospitality. Any who approach peaceably and invoke the guest-right are welcome to eat their food and shelter under their roof (such that it is). The Witches will do no true harm unless the guest first violates the rules of hospitality by…
E	initiating violence;
E	threatening the Witches or their guests;
E	stealing; or
E	insulting the Witches' hospitality.
P	The Witches delight in provoking guests:
P	speaking in riddles, asking about shameful secrets, offering disgusting victuals or shabby accommodations, showing glimpses of horrors that are gone when one looks again. The humble, patient, and wise do well. Hot-headed, prideful fools do not.
H3	The price
P	Whatever one asks of the Willow Witches, they require something of similar value.
P	Tailor the price to the character. It's not about what the Willow Witches want or what they'll do with it. It's about sacrifice.
P	It's about what the seeker is asking for, and what it's worth to them.
P	The Witches might ask for…
E	<b>a promise, to be fulfilled now or later</b>. Renege, and calamity follows. "The axiom of local contagion? Such fancy words for so simple a thing. We can teach you, yes, but you must swear to never again open a door without its owner's permission."
PAGE	121
E	<b>a possession, worth at least as much</b> <b>to the asker as that which they ask for</b>.
P	"You seek a weapon against the demon?
P	Ah, yes, the Twisted Spear! We can show you where it lies, take you to it. But what will you give us in return? That mantle you wear, the one with teeth and the hungry ghosts? Give us that."
E	<b>something strange, fraught with potential consequence</b>. "You seek to appease the anger of the forest? Tsk tsk, its anger cannot be quelled. But you can throw off the scent. Merely chew off your own shadow and let us dispose of it. Hmm? No, of course you can, here, let us show you…"
E	<b>a personal sacrifice, bloody and</b> <b>visceral</b>. "You wish to know what the old runes say? Surely your right eye is a bargain for such wisdom. Or the left.
P	We are not picky."
E	<b>a personal sacrifice, something</b> <b>intangible</b>. Work with the player to change their instinct, swap their stats, or lose one of their moves as a result.
P	"You seek a way to defeat the King of the North? We can tell you, yes. But it will cost the memories of your father, and the kindness he showed you."
E	<b>a sacrifice, but of something not</b> <b>truly theirs to give.</b> "You want your eye for beauty back? Hm. You choose the price: your tall friend's kind heart, which you treasure so. Or your parents' love. It's beauty you seek, and like must pay for like, after all."
P	Whatever the PCs ask for, it should be a meaningful decision whether they pay the price. Don't ask for something you know they'll never give up, and don't ask for something they won't miss anyhow.
P	If the Witches like someone—if they've been humble, well-mannered, and wise—then they'll be clear and upfront about the costs and what they're offering, and maybe suggest another course of action. Otherwise, the Witches will be cagey about the costs and all too willing to let them have something for cheap if they know that it will lead to ruin.

P	<i>Group</i>, <i>primordial</i>, <i>cautious</i>, <i>devious</i>, <i>organized</i>, <i>magical</i>, <i>all-wise</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 16; <b>Armor</b> 4 (wards, resilience), 0 vs.
P	black iron <b>Damage</b> gnarled fists and fingers d10+2 w/ disadvantage (<i>hand</i>, <i>forceful</i>, <i>grabby</i>)
P	<b>Special Qualities</b> impossible to deceive or surprise; divide damage taken equally between the three witches (round down)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to enforce the old ways, the old rules
P	• Frustrate, annoy, or provoke someone
P	• Twist someone's perceptions
P	• Vanish, be elsewhere
P	• Turn someone into a swamp creature
P	<b>Tip:</b> use a different voice and different physical position (left, center, right) for each witch, and shift between them as you talk, sometimes mid-sentence.
P	When you <b><i>press or entice the Willow Witches into changing their price or altering their</i></b> <b><i>deal</i></b>, don't roll. They will not be budged; the price is what it is.

B	Fallen logs or furrows hidden by grass or mud

B	Fog and mist, or blanketing snow, obscuring all of the above and worse

H3	Swarms
B	Midges or mosquitos—annoying, distracting, painful, diseased
B	Leeches—clinging to anything that gets in water
B	Starlings—obscuring, drowning out sound, buffeting, possibly possessed by a <b>grwgnach</b> (page 370)

ICON	icons/danger.svg
H3	Disease
P	Sickness can come from bad water, bad air, tainted food, and blood-sucking vermin. It's especially risky to have open wounds—in these conditions, it's all too easy for them to go rotten.
P	• Show that they've been exposed/infected
P	• Hit them with minor symptoms (mark <i>miserable</i>)
P	• Have symptoms worsen (mark another debility)
P	• Deny them rest
P	The best treatment for disease is rest, clean food, water, and air, and treatment with the proper herbs. Someone who pushes on through serious symptoms is likely Defying Danger (the danger that being that they get worse, or suffer complications).
P	To name a disease, or describe its symptoms, mix and match 2-3 of the following:
P	ague, angry, black, blisters, blood, blue, boils, breath, burning, chills, cold, cough, cramps, crows, dry, eye(s), festering, fever, fingers, fluttering, flux, foot, itching, lung, midge, milky, mouth, muddy, oozing, phlegm, pickled, pink, pox, rash, retching, rot, running, runs, scalp, shakes, shivers, skin, snot, sores, spit, spots, sweats, tears, tick, toad, toes, tongue, tremor, trots, warts, weed, weeping, welts, wet, wheezing, wound, yellow
P	Consider rolling the Die of Fate to see how serious the symptoms are and how hard the disease is to treat.
P	<b>Something interesting:</b> You know what this disease is called, its symptoms and typical course, maybe even what causes it. <b>Something</b> <b>useful:</b> You know how best to treat it, what herbs to use and where they might be found.

H3	Fen blight
P	Threat (<i>affliction</i>)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to strip away its victim's humanity
P	Those who spend significant time in Ferrier's Fen might find themselves… changed.
P	Marshedgers tell many tales about what causes the blight, and what will protect from it, but even the most careful fen-walker will sometimes start to feel the changes.
C	Little things, easy enough to hide, like warty skin, thinning hair, fetid odor, a lengthening tongue, a taste for bugs and snails
C	More pronounced changes, growing appetite, jealousy, a fear of being discovered
C	Growth spurts, increased strength, more obvious mutations, resentment towards the unafflicted
C	Difficulty with language, unending hunger, paranoia, urge to hide from sight
C	<b>Impending doom:</b> Transformation into a <b>fen-troll</b> (right)
H3	Monsters
B	Beasts from the <b>Great Wood</b> (page 200), often mutated
B	<b>Fae</b> (page 94), especially those who delight in ugliness and misfortune
B	<b>Spirits of the wild</b> (page 356)
B	<b>Green Lord</b> remnants (page 210), especially chimerae and hazardous growth
B	<b>Llamudwr</b> (page 220)
B	Spirits or beasts <b>corrupted</b> by the Things Below (page 432)
B	<b>Ghosts</b> (page 76) of those who died here, lost and alone
B	A rotting <b>pyped</b> (page 82), living on carrion and bog-bodies

H3	Fen-troll
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>large</i>, <i>corrupted</i>, <i>hoarder</i>, <i>gluttonous</i>, <i>stealthy</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 16; <b>Armor</b> 1 (thick hide)
P	<b>Damage</b> bone-snapping grip d10+3 (<i>hand</i>, <i>close</i>, <i>grabby</i>, <i>forceful</i>), rending maw d10+3 (<i>hand</i>, <i>messy</i>, 1 piercing)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> sharp senses, horrid odor, ashamed of its visage <b>Instinct</b> to fill its belly and jealously guard its hoard
P	• Approach a victim from cover of dark, or fog, or murky water
P	• Demand treasure to let them pass unharmed
P	• Probably try to eat them anyway
P	They were human once, corrupted by the Fen and the foul forces flowing through it.
P	Little remains of that humanity, though:
P	a rough shape, half-forgotten words, a terrible anger at what it has lost.
P	They prize finery and mundane goods, anything that reminds them of their former life. Even more, they long for human connection. But hunger, shame, and greed usually lead them to lash out at any who show them kindness.

P	<b>Special qualities</b> heals injuries in a few hours, regenerates limbs in a few days <b>Instinct</b> to eat pretty much anything

P	An enormous albino crayfish, older than the Fen itself. If you encounter it, pray it's not hungry. But fat chance of that.

ICON	icons/danger.svg
H3	Snaplilies
P	<b>Damage</b> snapping "jaws" 1d4 (<i>hand</i>, <i>grabby</i>)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to latch on and drag down
P	• Blend in with a field of lily pads
P	• Snap shut on a frog or bird, disappearing before anyone sees
P	• Snap tight on a limb, yank down
P	• SNAP SNAP SNAP on someone who trips and falls among them: 1d8 damage w/advantage (<i>grabby</i>, <i>messy</i>)
P	They blend right in, really. But when anything bigger'n a bug lands on one, SNAP, just like a bear trap, the vine contracting and pulling prey underwater. It's a lethal trap for a small creature. For a human?
P	Just a painful mistake. Unless you panic, of course, or flail, or trip. So just, you know, stay calm.
ICON	icons/beast.svg
H3	Suarachan hunters
P	<i>Group</i>, <i>stealthy</i>, <i>cautious</i>, <i>organized</i>, <i>amphibious</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 6; <b>Armor</b> 1 (scaly hide)
P	<b>Damage</b> cudgel d8 (<i>close</i>, <i>crude</i>), snapping tongue d6 (<i>reach</i>), poison blowgun needles d6 (<i>near</i>)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> excellent night vision, salt burns their skin <b>Instinct</b> to bring home captives for sacrifice
P	• Surround their quarry unnoticed
P	• Leap a shocking distance
P	• Club someone senseless on the head
P	• Tie a fast knot
P	They're tall as a short man, hunched on too-long legs and too-long arms. A toadlike head juts forward from broad shoulders, the eyes entirely too big, the mouth entirely too wide. They're covered in moist scales and horn-like growths, and draped in belts and bandoliers of woven grass.
P	These are the suarachan most often encountered, the ones that raid Marshedge and the ones that fen-walkers most fear.
P	Truly, they spend more time fishing and hunting than seeking sacrifices, and they're just as happy to claim a deer as a man. But deer are harder to catch, on the whole.
PAGE	125
HR
ICON	icons/beast.svg
H3	Suarachan singers
P	<i>Horde</i>, <i>amphibious</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 3; <b>Armor</b> 0 <b>Damage</b> fists and bite d6 w/ disadvantage (<i>hand</i>), snapping tongue d4 w/ disadvantage (<i>reach</i>)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> excellent night vision, salt burns their skin, mutations <b>Instinct</b> to sing the eternal lullaby
P	• Drown out all other noises with their song
P	• Raise a shrill call of alarm
P	• Scuttle away and hide
P	• Keep a prisoner living, long enough
P	There are places in Ferrier's Fen where horrors sleep, where the Things Below dream unquiet. The air in these places thrums with frog-song, so deep and so loud you can barely hear yourself think. But it's not frogs singing. It's the suarachan.
P	The suarachan believe that their songs keep the Things Below quiet. And they hope that their sacrifices—given in bulk in late autumn—will keep their dark gods satiated while the suarachan sleep through winter.
P	Most suarachan bear mutations: extra legs (often twisted and useless), overgrown or atrophied limbs, missing or extra eyes, strange growths, etc. The most mobile become hunters, but the chorus welcomes any suarachan that can sing.
ICON	icons/beast.svg
H3	Suarachan soothsayer
P	<i>Solitary</i>, <i>corrupted</i>, <i>cunning</i>, <i>magical</i>, <i>amphibious</i>
P	<b>HP</b> 12; <b>Armor</b> 0 <b>Damage</b> poisonous skin d10 (<i>hand</i>), snapping tongue d4 (<i>reach</i>)
P	<b>Special qualities</b> excellent night vision, salt burns their skin, marked by the Things Below (page 432)
P	<b>Instinct</b> to mollify the Things Below
P	• Secrete various poisons: debilitating, hallucinogenic, deadly
P	• Commune with outsiders via poison-induced visions
P	• Use a gift of the Things Below (page 432)
P	A few suarachan—one or two per chorus—have bright, colorful scales that ooze with slime. They will often ingest their own hallucinatory toxins, communing with the horrors that lay sleeping, shushing them and soothing them, and promising them meals of screaming flesh, soon, soon.
P	The suarachan lack language, per se. They can communicate basic concepts via their songs, but true communication requires a soothsayer's touch.
P	When you <b><i>are affected by the hallucinogenic poison of a suarachan soothsayer</i></b>, you can perceive spirits around you and speak to those who are active, as well as others affected by the poison. When the poison wears off, mark a debility (<i>dazed</i> if it's available).
